bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Return ratios disclosed for FY26: RoCE pre-tax 25%, RoE 20% and CFO/EBITDA 80% (RoCE defined as (PBIT ex Other income) / (Average Networth + Average Long Term Lease Liabilities - Average Surplus Cash)).
- Surplus cash of INR 2,869 Mn as at Mar-26 (from INR 2,067 Mn at Mar-25); the balance sheet shows non-current and current borrowings at 0 across Mar-22 to Mar-26, with lease liabilities of INR 4,000 Mn non-current at Mar-26.
- Growth is self-funded from operations: FY26 net cash from operating activities INR 2,706 Mn against purchase and construction of property, plant and building (net) of INR 1,827 Mn and cash flow from financing activities of INR -695 Mn.
- Shareholding as at 30 June 2026: Promoter & Promoter Group 52.5%, DIIs 31.6%, FIIs 11.7%, Others 4.2%.
- Inorganic capital deployment precedent: acquisition of subsidiary outflow of INR 1,475 Mn in FY24, tied to the 100% acquisition of P.H. Diagnostics and entry into Pune.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Integrated diagnostics platform combining pathology and radiology on a single platform, improving service utilisation and driving operating leverage from shared infrastructure, technology and resources
- Strong B2C franchise and brand equity, with approximately 92% of revenue derived from the B2C segment, giving revenue stability and deeper customer engagement
- Expanding multi-state network across Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra, West Bengal, Karnataka and the NCR, with densification driving operating leverage
- Technology and digital capabilities: advanced diagnostic equipment, AI-enabled radiology solutions, LIMS, RIS, PACS, digital reporting and an integrated teleradiology platform ensuring standardised reporting protocols
- Growing wellness and preventive healthcare portfolio, with wellness contributing 14.8% of revenue in FY26, driving higher average revenue per patient
- Operational excellence through the hub-and-spoke model, driving throughput, process standardisation and faster turnaround times
- Experienced clinical talent pool of more than 400 specialised and super-specialised radiologists and pathologists, many from top tier medical institutions
- Strong financial position with a strong balance sheet, healthy return profile and disciplined capital allocation providing flexibility to invest in network expansion
- Over four decades of operating experience, with the core Hyderabad market growing in double digits and gaining share from the unorganised sector
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Competition risk — Intensifying competition from national chains, regional diagnostic players and hospital-based laboratories may impact market share and pricing. Mitigation is to strengthen brand visibility, deepen customer engagement, expand network density and leverage the integrated diagnostics model to differentiate service offerings.
- Expansion and integration risk — Delays in scaling new geographies or integrating acquired businesses may impact growth and profitability. This is structurally significant given the Company commissioned 10 hub centres across four geographies in FY26 and plans 8-9 hubs and 10-12 spokes in FY27. Mitigation is a phased expansion strategy, standardised operating protocols and close monitoring of integration milestones, project execution and centre-level performance.
- Technology and quality risk — Equipment downtime, reporting inaccuracies, delays in technology adoption or technology failures may affect service quality and patient trust. Mitigation is investment in advanced diagnostic technologies, stringent quality assurance protocols and periodic equipment calibration and maintenance.
- Regulatory risk — Changes in healthcare regulations, accreditation requirements or compliance standards may impact operations. Mitigation is robust compliance processes, periodic audits and monitoring of regulatory developments across operating markets.
- Talent risk — Shortage or attrition of skilled radiologists, pathologists and healthcare professionals may affect service delivery. Mitigation is strengthened talent acquisition, investment in training and professional development and retention-focused incentive programmes.
- Cybersecurity and patient data risk — Cyberattacks or data breaches may compromise patient information and disrupt operations. Mitigation is enhanced cybersecurity infrastructure, periodic vulnerability assessments, employee awareness programmes and strengthened data governance and protection protocols.
- Operational continuity risk — Disruptions arising from utility outages, natural disasters, workforce shortages or other unforeseen events may affect service continuity. Mitigation is business continuity plans, operational redundancies and contingency arrangements for critical functions.
- Supply chain risk — Dependence on suppliers for diagnostic equipment, consumables and reagents may lead to procurement disruptions. Mitigation is diversified supplier relationships, optimised inventory levels and sourcing redundancies for critical supplies.
- Reputation risk — Service quality issues or adverse patient experiences may impact brand reputation and customer confidence, which matters given approximately 92% of revenue is B2C and dependent on direct consumer trust. Mitigation is maintaining high clinical standards and monitoring service quality metrics.

business.body:
- Described as "the largest integrated B2C focused diagnostic chain in India with 166 state-of-the-art centres spread across 27 cities & towns"; founded by Mr. Surendranath Reddy in 1981, currently led by Ms. Suprita Reddy, with 40+ years of vintage and 350+ doctors in the radiologist & pathologist network.
- Integrated one-stop offering combining pathology and radiology under one roof; deck states revenue mix for Q1 FY27 of Pathology 62.8% / Radiology 37.2%.
- "Dominant Position in Telangana & AP Markets with a Strong Brand Recall" — the deck says a dense network across AP & Telangana "aids in distributing patient load and offering significantly faster TAT across tests".
- B2C revenue share of ~92%; the deck attributes "Industry leading margins" to the "Integrated business model with high B2C concentration (~92%) and a strong brand recall".
- Home collections and online/app/call-centre booking are presented as accessibility and stickiness drivers, with samples reaching the lab "within 2 hours" post collection under temperature-controlled logistics.

business.body:

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Disciplined, phased network expansion under a hub-and-spoke operating model with a concentric-circle approach, deepening presence in existing markets while building scale in newer ones
- Expand into new geographies, particularly Tier-II cities and semi-urban clusters, where demand for organised high-quality diagnostics continues to grow
- Deepen presence across additional districts in West Bengal following the encouraging response in Tier-2 districts
- Entering each new market with advanced 3T MRI technology and a fully integrated radiology and pathology offering, so quality is not diluted by the pace of expansion
- Continue investing in advanced diagnostic technologies, automation, specialised testing capabilities and digital infrastructure to support the next phase of sustainable growth
- Maintain the four guiding pillars of the business: relentless focus on quality and customer experience; continuous investment in technology while ensuring affordability; sustainable growth through disciplined network expansion; and investment in talent
- Grow the wellness and preventive-healthcare portfolio through curated preventive health packages on the integrated radiology and pathology platform
- Sustain the B2C-led model and brand franchise, gaining market share from the unorganised sector in core markets such as Hyderabad
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: FY26 was described as a landmark year in which the Company executed one of the most ambitious network expansion programmes in its history, commissioning 10 hub centres across four geographies within a single financial year, each entered with advanced 3T MRI technology and a fully integrated radiology and pathology offering. Expansion into Tier-2 districts of West Bengal was singled out as particularly significant, with several centres ramping up faster than anticipated and management stating an intent to deepen presence across additional districts in the state in the years ahead. New hub centres were commissioned in Khammam and Nandyal, tier-2 towns in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh, while Hyderabad and the core markets grew in double digits without new hub additions. The flagship Bengaluru hub, spanning over 10,000 sq. ft. and housing advanced radiology equipment alongside a comprehensive pathology laboratory, was a key milestone, following the 2025 launch of two hub centres in Yelahanka and HSR Layout. For FY27 management plans to commission 8-9 hub centres and 10-12 spoke centres across the network. The network stood at 162 centres across 27 cities and towns in six states as on 31 March 2026, having doubled from 81 centres across 3 states at the time of listing in 2021. Ongoing investment continues in newer-generation equipment such as wide-bore 3T MRI and digital PET-CT with advanced cardiac CT capabilities, AI-assisted imaging, and expanded access to dental diagnostics and CT KUB services across the network. Management describes the expansion strategy as asset-light and disciplined, supported by a strong balance sheet and healthy cash generation.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Favourable demographics, rising disposable incomes, increasing urbanisation and greater healthcare awareness continue to support demand for healthcare and diagnostic services
- Rising healthcare awareness, increasing prevalence of lifestyle-related diseases, expanding health insurance coverage and greater adoption of preventive healthcare are expected to support long-term demand for organised diagnostic services
- India's diagnostic services market is expected to expand at a CAGR of approximately 12% over the next five years, reaching an estimated market size of USD 15-16 billion
- Diagnostics companies recorded revenue growth of 10-22% in FY 2025-26, with EBITDA margins ranging between 25 and 35%, driven by expansion into smaller cities, increasing consumer engagement and the introduction of advanced tests across genomics and AI-based diagnostics
- Diagnostic laboratories account for less than 10% of India's overall healthcare expenditure, with demand driven by preventive healthcare, chronic disease management and data-driven clinical decision-making
- Industry consolidation, technology adoption and expansion into Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities are expected to support long-term growth, although new facilities may face short-term profitability pressures
- Healthcare allocation in the Union Budget 2026-27 increased to INR 1,06,530 crores, nearly 10% higher than the Revised Estimates for FY 2025-26
- India's healthcare sector recorded transactions exceeding INR 10,000 crore across hospitals, diagnostics and specialty care segments during FY 2025-26, driven by private equity investors and strategic buyers focusing on scalable platforms and technology-enabled delivery models
- Improving healthcare infrastructure, with hospital bed availability at nearly 1.6 per 1,000 population and doctor density at about 1.23 per 1,000
- India's real GDP grew by an estimated 7.6% in FY 2026 and is projected at 6.6% in FY 2027, with inflation projected at a manageable 4.6% in FY 2027, supporting macroeconomic stability
- Global GDP growth is projected to moderate to 3.1% in CY 2026 before improving marginally to 3.2% in CY 2027, with geopolitical risks, evolving trade policies and financial market volatility continuing to influence global growth
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Vijaya Diagnostic delivered a landmark Q4FY26 with 26.6% revenue growth and 379 bps EBITDA margin expansion to 43.5%, driven by volume-led growth (18.5%) and rapid breakeven of new hubs. Management guides for continued double-digit growth in FY27 with conservative 40%+ margins despite increased capex for density and technology upgrades.

currentContext.expansion: FY26 was described as a landmark year in which the Company executed one of the most ambitious network expansion programmes in its history, commissioning 10 hub centres across four geographies within a single financial year, each entered with advanced 3T MRI technology and a fully integrated radiology and pathology offering. Expansion into Tier-2 districts of West Bengal was singled out as particularly significant, with several centres ramping up faster than anticipated and management stating an intent to deepen presence across additional districts in the state in the years ahead. New hub centres were commissioned in Khammam and Nandyal, tier-2 towns in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh, while Hyderabad and the core markets grew in double digits without new hub additions. The flagship Bengaluru hub, spanning over 10,000 sq. ft. and housing advanced radiology equipment alongside a comprehensive pathology laboratory, was a key milestone, following the 2025 launch of two hub centres in Yelahanka and HSR Layout. For FY27 management plans to commission 8-9 hub centres and 10-12 spoke centres across the network. The network stood at 162 centres across 27 cities and towns in six states as on 31 March 2026, having doubled from 81 centres across 3 states at the time of listing in 2021. Ongoing investment continues in newer-generation equipment such as wide-bore 3T MRI and digital PET-CT with advanced cardiac CT capabilities, AI-assisted imaging, and expanded access to dental diagnostics and CT KUB services across the network. Management describes the expansion strategy as asset-light and disciplined, supported by a strong balance sheet and healthy cash generation.

risks.note: Intensifying competition from national chains, regional diagnostic players and hospital-based laboratories may impact market share and pricing. Mitigation is to strengthen brand visibility, deepen customer engagement, expand network density and leverage the integrated diagnostics model to differentiate service offerings.

Delays in scaling new geographies or integrating acquired businesses may impact growth and profitability. This is structurally significant given the Company commissioned 10 hub centres across four geographies in FY26 and plans 8-9 hubs and 10-12 spokes in FY27. Mitigation is a phased expansion strategy, standardised operating protocols and close monitoring of integration milestones, project execution and centre-level performance.

Equipment downtime, reporting inaccuracies, delays in technology adoption or technology failures may affect service quality and patient trust. Mitigation is investment in advanced diagnostic technologies, stringent quality assurance protocols and periodic equipment calibration and maintenance.

Changes in healthcare regulations, accreditation requirements or compliance standards may impact operations. Mitigation is robust compliance processes, periodic audits and monitoring of regulatory developments across operating markets.

Shortage or attrition of skilled radiologists, pathologists and healthcare professionals may affect service delivery. Mitigation is strengthened talent acquisition, investment in training and professional development and retention-focused incentive programmes.

Cyberattacks or data breaches may compromise patient information and disrupt operations. Mitigation is enhanced cybersecurity infrastructure, periodic vulnerability assessments, employee awareness programmes and strengthened data governance and protection protocols.

Disruptions arising from utility outages, natural disasters, workforce shortages or other unforeseen events may affect service continuity. Mitigation is business continuity plans, operational redundancies and contingency arrangements for critical functions.

Dependence on suppliers for diagnostic equipment, consumables and reagents may lead to procurement disruptions. Mitigation is diversified supplier relationships, optimised inventory levels and sourcing redundancies for critical supplies.

Service quality issues or adverse patient experiences may impact brand reputation and customer confidence, which matters given approximately 92% of revenue is B2C and dependent on direct consumer trust. Mitigation is maintaining high clinical standards and monitoring service quality metrics.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Favourable demographics, rising disposable incomes, increasing urbanisation and greater healthcare awareness continue to support demand for healthcare and diagnostic services
- Rising healthcare awareness, increasing prevalence of lifestyle-related diseases, expanding health insurance coverage and greater adoption of preventive healthcare are expected to support long-term demand for organised diagnostic services
- India's diagnostic services market is expected to expand at a CAGR of approximately 12% over the next five years, reaching an estimated market size of USD 15-16 billion
- Diagnostics companies recorded revenue growth of 10-22% in FY 2025-26, with EBITDA margins ranging between 25 and 35%, driven by expansion into smaller cities, increasing consumer engagement and the introduction of advanced tests across genomics and AI-based diagnostics
- Diagnostic laboratories account for less than 10% of India's overall healthcare expenditure, with demand driven by preventive healthcare, chronic disease management and data-driven clinical decision-making
- Industry consolidation, technology adoption and expansion into Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities are expected to support long-term growth, although new facilities may face short-term profitability pressures
- Healthcare allocation in the Union Budget 2026-27 increased to INR 1,06,530 crores, nearly 10% higher than the Revised Estimates for FY 2025-26
- India's healthcare sector recorded transactions exceeding INR 10,000 crore across hospitals, diagnostics and specialty care segments during FY 2025-26, driven by private equity investors and strategic buyers focusing on scalable platforms and technology-enabled delivery models
- Improving healthcare infrastructure, with hospital bed availability at nearly 1.6 per 1,000 population and doctor density at about 1.23 per 1,000
- India's real GDP grew by an estimated 7.6% in FY 2026 and is projected at 6.6% in FY 2027, with inflation projected at a manageable 4.6% in FY 2027, supporting macroeconomic stability
- Global GDP growth is projected to moderate to 3.1% in CY 2026 before improving marginally to 3.2% in CY 2027, with geopolitical risks, evolving trade policies and financial market volatility continuing to influence global growth

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: FY26 was described as a landmark year in which the Company executed one of the most ambitious network expansion programmes in its history, commissioning 10 hub centres across four geographies within a single financial year, each entered with advanced 3T MRI technology and a fully integrated radiology and pathology offering. Expansion into Tier-2 districts of West Bengal was singled out as particularly significant, with several centres ramping up faster than anticipated and management stating an intent to deepen presence across additional districts in the state in the years ahead. New hub centres were commissioned in Khammam and Nandyal, tier-2 towns in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh, while Hyderabad and the core markets grew in double digits without new hub additions. The flagship Bengaluru hub, spanning over 10,000 sq. ft. and housing advanced radiology equipment alongside a comprehensive pathology laboratory, was a key milestone, following the 2025 launch of two hub centres in Yelahanka and HSR Layout. For FY27 management plans to commission 8-9 hub centres and 10-12 spoke centres across the network. The network stood at 162 centres across 27 cities and towns in six states as on 31 March 2026, having doubled from 81 centres across 3 states at the time of listing in 2021. Ongoing investment continues in newer-generation equipment such as wide-bore 3T MRI and digital PET-CT with advanced cardiac CT capabilities, AI-assisted imaging, and expanded access to dental diagnostics and CT KUB services across the network. Management describes the expansion strategy as asset-light and disciplined, supported by a strong balance sheet and healthy cash generation.

financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 219cr (+26.6% YoY); EBITDA: INR 95.5cr (+38.7% YoY), Margin 43.5% (+379bps); PAT: INR 47.9cr (+37.5% YoY); Order Book: N/A (Service model); Net Debt: Net Cash (INR 280-300cr cash balance). One-offs: Favorable seasonality and faster-than-expected breakeven of new hubs (Khammam, Nandyal in 2 quarters vs 3 guided) drove margin beat.
guidance: Revenue Growth: Double-digit (volume-led); Margin: Conservative guidance >40% (vs Q4's 43.5%); Order Inflow: Organic hub/spoke addition; Capex: INR 140-150cr for FY27 (includes automated lab).
order book & pipeline: N/A - Service revenue model based on footfall and test volumes.
segment / subsidiary detail: Pathology & Radiology mix ~50:50 in wellness bundles; Radiology contributes 37% of total revenue; B2C mix remains dominant at 92%; Hyderabad contributes 67% of revenue with 20% growth.
growth verticals / optionality: Density play in existing 6 states (adding 4-5 hubs, 10-12 spokes in FY27); Automated lab in Panjagutta for productivity; Genomics as long-term specialized offering; Potential inorganic M&A if valuation/ethos aligns.
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin expanded to 43.5% due to operating leverage on fixed cost base and rapid breakeven of new centers (OPEX burn only 0.8% vs expected 2-2.5%). Cost heads: Consumables/doctors variable; Rent/tech/talent fixed. Digital marketing spend doubling to INR 12-14cr.
capex / expansion: FY26 Actual: INR 169cr; FY27 Guidance: INR 140-150cr. Breakup: INR 120-130cr for 4-5 hubs & 10-12 spokes (executed leases); INR 10-12cr replacement/modality capex; Remainder for state-of-the-art automated lab in Panjagutta.
capital allocation: Organic expansion prioritized (dense network in AP, Telangana, Pune, WB, Karnataka); Cash balance INR 280-300cr available for opportunistic M&A (8-15 assets reviewed annually) but no immediate cluster additions planned outside current 6 states.
risks & watch-items: Execution risk on new geography ramp-up; Competition from hospital labs (mitigated by price/experience diff); Regulatory approvals for AI/Genomics; Talent retention in new markets.
management quality / tone: Confident yet conservative on guidance; Disciplined on capital allocation; Focused on quality/talent over aggressive geographic sprawl; Transparent on breakeven timelines.
non-obvious takeaways: New hubs in core markets breakeven in 2 quarters vs 3 guided; Hyderabad mature market still growing at 20% due to density/market share gains; Wellness realization per patient rises while per-test realization dips due to bundle mix.

| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |

themes.title: Hospitals, diagnostics & domestic healthcare
themes.need: Under-bedded India plus insurance penetration and preventive-care adoption drive a domestic healthcare capex + volume cycle distinct from export pharma. MAXHEALTH adding ~2,500+ beds (Gurgaon 500-bed by FY27); APOLLOHOSP/MEDANTA/KIMS/NH/ASTERDM/MAXHEALTH on hospitals; LALPATHLAB/METROPOLIS/THYROCARE/VIJAYA on diagnostics (LALPATHLAB guides 13-15% FY27); MEDPLUS/ENTERO on pharmacy/distribution; POLYMED on devices. The same India-only demand engine now also carries India-facing branded pharma, which is driven by domestic volume and price rather than the export book: GLAXO delivered its first INR 1,000cr quarter with 8.1% revenue growth, Shingrix at a ~INR 75cr annual run-rate (CY25, +80% YoY) and Jemperli's first-line approval expanding eligible patients from 800 to 6,000; ERIS (dermatology 15% of revenue after INR 1,265cr of domestic brand acquisitions), SANOFI (India-for-India, NLEM price cuts) and THEMISMED (hospital segment +20% YoY) sit on the same axis.
themes.driver: New-bed commissioning + occupancy ramp; Tier 3/4 diagnostics penetration; CGHS rate revision; preventive-test volumes; domestic branded-formulation volume growth and NLEM/price actions.

hero.oneLiner: Vijaya Diagnostic Centre Limited is an integrated diagnostic chain, established in 1981 and headquartered in Hyderabad, operating 162 centres across six states with pathology and radiology delivered on a single platform.
